cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: That lecture from the visiting speaker yesterday was good, wasn't it?

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: Yeah. I learned a lot from her about ocean biodiversity. I've already done some reading on it, and I did an assignment on some of the problems associated with it last year, but I especially liked the way her lecture focused on more long-term issues. (Q21/Q22)

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Yes, things that aren't currently receiving widespread attention but are likely to be important in the future. That impressed me too. It wasn't exactly a feel-good conclusion because it's hard to see any real solution for a lot of the problems.

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: No, though she did point to where policy changes could be made to protect our marine and coastal environments.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Mm. But that's just at a national level. The examples she gave were at a more global level, and they really made it clear to me just how wide-ranging the threats to ocean biodiversity are. (Q21/Q22)

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: Yes, me too.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: The research project she described was impressive, wasn't it? I'd have thought it was quite unusual to have so many experts working together. (Q23/Q24)

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: Yeah, and from such different backgrounds. Must have been a really exciting team to work with. I'd heard of a couple of them before – they were involved in research way back in 2009 warning about the dangers of ocean pollution. (Q23/Q24)

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: But now people are much more aware of that, aren't they?

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: I suppose so.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Another thing about the research is that the team members came from all round the world. Though I suppose that's not unusual nowadays, now everyone can work remotely.

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: Right. I liked the way she didn't bombard us with figures – I mean, they were available, but she focused more on the general points they indicated.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Mm. And the description of improvements in systems used for tracking marine animals and things like robots were really interesting. (Q23/Q24)

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: Yes, and her description of how robotics can be used to investigate threats to biodiversity.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Absolutely.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: While you're here, can we talk about the list of resources we have to evaluate for the seminar tomorrow. I've had a look at them all, but it's been a bit of a rush.

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: Yeah. What did you think of that article on invasive lionfish? The one claiming they were expanding their habitat throughout the Mediterranean Sea.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Well, the writer went on about how dangerous they were in environmental terms, which is probably true, but he didn't really provide much information to explain why. (Q25)

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: I know what you mean.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: I watched the documentary on microplastics, at least I started to, but then I found it was made ten years ago so I gave up.

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: I watched to the end but you're right, it was showing its age. People had hardly heard of microplastics then, whereas now everyone knows about them and how dangerous they are. (Q26)

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Yeah. Did you listen to the podcast on ocean pollution?

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: Mm. I didn't get anything out of it though. Most of it was stating the obvious.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Yes, it mentioned pesticides and plastic and things, and it clearly made the point that they were a bad thing, but everybody knows that anyway. Did you read that book on coastal ecosystems? (Q27)

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: The one by John Harper? Yes, I found it hard going at first, it went into a lot of detail about things like the effects of offshore windfarms and fish farms, but actually I ended up with a much better understanding of the issues.

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Yes, I agree and I thought it was a well-written summary of those. And the diagrams helped a lot too. (Q28)

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: The article on metal toxicity was way above my head, I didn't know anything about how metals from industrial emissions react in the ocean... and I still don't understand it. (Q29)

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: I gave up reading after the first chapter – I just couldn't follow it.

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: That podcast on floating marine cities was interesting, though it presented a rather one-sided picture, I thought. (Q30)

cues.speaker: PHIL
cues.text: Yes, it focused on how this would benefit people and ignored the effects on the environment.

cues.speaker: LUCY
cues.text: But anyway, shall we ...
